_comment: I0 law-enforcement playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). What the US Secret Service accepts from a victim or PI (a report to the nearest field office, by telephone; no e-mail or web form), what it can then send to whom, and the evidence it wants. A report is never a freeze; only the agent's request through the provider's LE channel, then a seizure warrant, moves the funds.
notes: USSS also points victims to IC3 (ic3.gov) and local police. Investigators may contact the victim for more information; a substantive reply comes from an agent naming a field office and a case number. Operation Atlantic (Washington Field Office) covers victims of crypto confidence scams, with UK and Canadian victims sent to their own national resources; its victim form is hosted off the USSS domain, so it is not catalogued.

usss.field-offices.notes: Report a financial crime or scam to the nearest field office; by telephone for immediate assistance. Time-sensitive information should not be sent by e-mail.

paths.notes: Give the investment websites, phone numbers, e-mails and social-media profiles, every crypto address, the transaction hashes and dates, and the trace report; file at IC3 too and quote its ID.

issues.notes: Freeze request through Tether's law-enforcement platform (USSS onboarded Dec 2023); many USSS seizures of crypto-confidence-scam proceeds were made with Tether's assistance.

issues.by: a federal magistrate on the agent's / AUSA's application
issues.notes: Then a civil forfeiture complaint and return to victims (months).

sources.title: USSS - Largest ever seizure of funds related to crypto confidence scams (2025)
